faultCodes.meaning: Power loss for two cycles. This may indicate that the unit power is "dirty" or is of low quality. None on 3-phase units. 1-phase units: IMC will cycle compressor off for 5 minutes (default).
likelyCauses: Poor-quality or intermittent line power, loose line-voltage connection
Brownouts or momentary outages
checks: Check line voltage and connections at the disconnect and unit terminal block (field practice)
Single-phase units: expect a 5-minute compressor off cycle after the event (manual)

faultCodes.meaning: ECTO access error. This may indicate a problem with the ECTO memory chip and parameters may not be changeable. Control will operate with the factory ECTO defaults.

checks: Verify ECTO settings can still be read/changed; if not, replace the ECTO chip/board per Lennox (manual)

faultCodes.meaning: A17 input indicates smoke alarm. Defined by ECTO 5.01. Default action unit off.
likelyCauses: Smoke detector (A17) tripped or its output relay/wiring open

faultCodes.meaning: S52 (Air Flow Switch) This indicates no blower air 16 seconds after blower demand. Blower will cycle with demand unless ECTO 6.17 is set to 1. In that case the blower will operate continuously during occupied periods and will cycle with demands during unoccupied periods.
likelyCauses: Blower not running: belt, motor, contactor, overload
Air flow switch S52 or tubing/wiring fault
checks: Confirm blower rotation and belt condition, then check S52 and its tubing/wiring (field practice)

faultCodes.meaning: A42, S42, or S149 input is open between TB1-6 & TB1-23. A42 is a phase monitor; S42 is blower overload or inverter fault output; S149 is condensate overflow switch. Unit off.
likelyCauses: Phase loss/reversal (A42)
Blower overload or VFD fault (S42)
Condensate overflow (S149)
Open wiring between TB1-6 and TB1-23
checks: Check phase monitor status, blower motor overload/VFD fault, and the condensate pan/overflow switch, then the TB1-6 to TB1-23 loop (manual + field practice)

diagnosticTips: Where to look: the A55 (M1-7/M1-8) board in the unit control box carries a multi-digit LED readout, a single pushbutton, a green heartbeat LED and MODE DIP switches (UNIT TEST, RECALL, ECTO, TEMP, OPT2, SHIFT). Active error codes are shown on the readout; every code is also stored for recall.

Read stored codes: set the MODE DIP RECALL switch ON, then short-push the pushbutton; stored codes display in reverse order (most recent first) with each short push. A zero means nothing is stored. Set RECALL back OFF when done.
Clear stored codes: with RECALL ON, hold the pushbutton down until 0 is displayed, then turn RECALL OFF.

Reset a lockout: two successive short pushes of the pushbutton reset counters, lockout conditions and timers (codes marked "locked off/locked out" - 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25, 27, 29, 33, 35, 37, 39, 51, 53, 55, 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, 67, 69, 109). A control power reset does the same. Fix the root cause first; manual-reset rollout switches (S47/S69) must be reset at the switch.
A single push of the pushbutton advances to the next display; a double push returns to the previous display (used in ECTO/TEMP modes).

Unit test: the UNIT TEST DIP switch / "Testing Unit Function" section lets the IMC drive individual outputs (blower, compressors, fans, reversing valve, service relay) to check components; thermostat demands can also be simulated by jumpering TB1-6 to TB1-3 (blower), TB1-18 (Y1), TB1-12 (Y2) or TB1-2 (W1). A short push of the pushbutton skips the current delay timer.
The service output (24 VAC alarm relay) is energized by default on the lockout errors marked with * in Table 4; this is what a BAS or remote light sees.

Trip counters: most "opened 3 (default) times" thresholds are set by ECTO parameters (e.g. 1.12/4.14 high pressure, 1.13/4.15 freezestat, 4.04, 3.04, 3.09); a unit configured with a different count will lock out sooner or later than the table states.
The IMC ignores the low-pressure switches during compressor start-up, so a stored low-pressure code (22-29) reflects a real trip after the delay.

Sensor codes 73-78 and 91-99: RT6/RT16/RT17 are 2-wire thermistors, A2 zone sensors are a 2-wire thermistor with a 1k series resistor; measure resistance at the board terminals against the temperature-resistance chart before replacing.

notes: Transcribed from the M1-7 Version 5.02 Table 4 IMC Error Codes via search-engine excerpts of the manualzz text index and the lennoxeurope PDF; the same code numbering is used on the M1-8 (Version 6 door label lists codes 1-127).

Coverage is "partial" because codes 103 and 105 could not be captured cleanly (search excerpts conflated them with 104 and 107) and codes 111-126 are reserved on the M1-7 but may be assigned on the M1-8 Version 6 label; all other codes 1-127 are included.
Meaning text follows the table wording as returned by search excerpts; a few action clauses (code 23 compressor number, code 47 action) were reconstructed and are flagged in the entry notes.
Earlier IMC versions (M1-4 through M1-6, IMC V4/V5/V6 manuals) use largely the same numbering but fewer codes; confirm against the version on the board label.
